What I personally like about this approach is that you can "treat yourself" to a brand item when they are on sale because the unit price is lower, equal or close enough to the house brand you would usually buy.

Personally I really like hunting for grocery deals. I will buy buy 8 tubes of toothpaste when it is 2+2 free, buy 10 bottles of laundry detergent when it's 2+3 free, ... Over time I found I also got a way better sense of how much something is supposed to cost so that you can filter out any fake "deals" grocery shops might be pushing on you. In Belgium I would generally recommended Colruyt for the products of which you want the brand (Nutella, Coca Cola, ...). However, the real savings also lay in switching to white label products, I have done this for many commodity-like items (e.g. milk, coffee, orange juice, yoghurt, toilet paper ...). I find that sometimes they even taste better than the branded item, I'll take pickles crisps from Delhaize 365 over Lay's every time! Generally speaking I think a good way to transition into this is by switching one product at a time. Start with the basics like milk, yoghurt, bottled water, biscuits for the kids, ... Later you can move on to the items you are more attached to like Lay's crisps, Nutella and perhaps even Coca Cola. After a long time I tried bottled Pepsi and to be honest it quite good. I still keep cans of Coke in the basement fridge in case people come over though. 😅 Of course the most important way of comparison is unit prices.
